title: Destructuring and spread/rest
learningObjectives: Explain destructuring and spread/rest and read or transform JavaScript data safely.

understand.concept: Destructuring extracts values from arrays or properties from objects into bindings. Spread syntax expands iterable values or object properties into a new array or object. Rest syntax collects remaining values into an array or object. Spread copies are shallow.
understand.whyItMatters: These features make data transformation concise, but shallow copies still share nested object references. Be deliberate when updating shared state.
understand.analogy: Destructuring unpacks a parcel into labelled items; spread lays out its contents, while rest collects what remains.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; JavaScript references, serialization, and DOM APIs have precise behaviour defined by the language and web platform.

explain.narrative: The object is destructured into name and score, spread creates a shallow updated object, and rest collects the remaining array items.

examples.explanation: The object is destructured into name and score, spread creates a shallow updated object, and rest collects the remaining array items.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console or page displays the selected, transformed, or serialized data.

practise.guidedTask: Destructure an object, create an updated copy with spread, and collect remaining function arguments using rest.
practise.independentTask: Build a small data-processing or DOM-selection example. Include missing-data handling and explain any shallow-copy or serialization limits.
hints: Check optional properties before accessing them.
Remember shallow copies share nested references.
Handle JSON parsing errors and validate data shape.

practice.starterCode:
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Destructuring and spread/rest</title></head><body>
<script>const learner={name:'Asha',level:'Beginner',score:80};const {name,score}=learner;const updated={...learner,score:90};const [first,...others]=['HTML','CSS','JavaScript'];console.log(name,score,updated,first,others);</script>
</body></html>

questions.prompt: Does object spread create a deep clone of nested objects?
questions.explanation: Spread creates a shallow copy; nested object references are shared.

questions.prompt: What is a safe approach when working with nested or external data?
options: Check structure and handle missing or invalid values
Use JSON parsing as schema validation
questions.answer: Check structure and handle missing or invalid values
questions.explanation: External data must be checked for expected shape and valid values.
